headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1951 p. 564 through A.L. 2016 S.B. 702). headings.title: Taxicab driver exclusion and IRS right-to-control exception

headings.title: General meaning of employment and federal tax coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1951 p. 564 through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.; Beal (1976) and Deutschmann (1977) annotations). Defines 'employment' as service for wages or under a contract of hire, including interstate commerce and services subject to or required to be covered under federal unemployment tax laws for full FUTA credit.

headings.title: Localized service and multistate coverage rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1)–(2)) and source notes. Includes an individual's entire service performed within or both within and without Missouri when localized in Missouri, or when non-localized service performed partly in Missouri has its base of operations, direction/control, or (if neither is in a service state) the individual's residence in Missouri. Independent review revised title so it covers service performed wholly within Missouri as well as multistate service tied to Missouri by localization, base of operations, direction/control, or residence.

headings.title: Service covered by election or reciprocal arrangement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1)–(2)) and source notes. Deems service for wages to be covered employment if covered by an approved election under § 288.080(3)(2) or an interstate or federal reciprocal arrangement under § 288.340 treating all services as performed in Missouri.

headings.title: When service is localized within a state
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Defines service as localized within a state when performed entirely there, or when out-of-state service is incidental (such as temporary, transitory, or isolated transactions).

headings.title: Independent contractor exception and right-to-control test
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Deems remunerated service to be covered employment unless shown to the division's satisfaction to be performed by an independent contractor under the common-law agency right-to-control test distinguishing control over manner and means versus results only.

headings.title: Agent-drivers, commission-drivers, and traveling or city salesmen
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (subdivisions (1)–(3)) and source notes. Includes specified product/laundry agent-drivers, commission-drivers, and full-time traveling or city salesmen soliciting business orders, conditioned on personal performance, no substantial non-transportation facility investment, and a continuing relationship.

headings.title: Service for state, political subdivisions, and instrumentalities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes. Includes service for Missouri, its political subdivisions, and wholly owned or multi-state instrumentalities when excluded from FUTA under 26 U.S.C. § 3306(c)(7) and not excluded under subsection 9.

headings.title: Service for Section 501(c)(3) nonprofit organizations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes. Includes service for religious, charitable, scientific, public-safety, literary, educational, cruelty-prevention, or other IRC § 501(c)(3) tax-exempt organizations employing four or more individuals on any day in 20 different calendar weeks.

headings.title: Exclusions from governmental and nonprofit employment coverage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 (subdivisions (1)–(7)) and source notes. Excludes from subsections 7 and 8 church/religious-organization staff, ministers and religious-order members, specified elected/legislative/judicial/Guard/emergency/policymaking governmental roles, rehabilitation facility workers, public work-relief/training participants, inmates, and enrolled students or qualifying financial-aid student spouses.

headings.title: Service by U.S. citizens outside the United States
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 (subdivisions (1)–(4)) and source notes. Covers U.S. citizens' service outside the United States (except Canada) based on Missouri principal place of business, Missouri employer residence/incorporation/majority partners or trustees, or election/claim criteria, and defines 'United States' for subsections 10 and 11.

headings.title: Definition of American employer for subsection 10
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 (subdivisions (1)–(4)) and source notes. Defines 'American employer' for purposes of subsection 10 as a U.S.-resident individual, a partnership with at least two-thirds U.S.-resident partners, a trust with all U.S.-resident trustees, or a U.S.- or state-organized corporation (retaining archived structure even though subsection 10 omits the phrase 'American employer').

headings.title: Enumerated employment exclusions and coverage exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 (subdivisions (1)–(18)) and source notes (including Beal (1976) and Deutschmann (1977) annotations). Lists 18 employment exclusions—including agricultural labor (with post-1977 $20,000/10-worker coverage exception and crew-leader rules; retains archived '12 U.S.C. 1441j' citation), domestic service, newspaper/magazine distribution, family employment, federal/foreign-government systems, student work, commission insurance agents, CETA, work-study, real estate licensees, direct sellers, and per-study research volunteers. Independent review revised title to clarify coverage exceptions across the 18 subdivisions (post-1977 agricultural labor, § 288.034(13) domestic service, required CETA coverage, and employer-established work-study programs) without ambiguous "agricultural exceptions" phrasing.

headings.title: Covered domestic service after December 31, 1977
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and source notes. Includes domestic service defined in subdivisions (2) and (13) of subsection 12 performed after December 31, 1977, if the employing unit paid $1,000 or more in cash wages for such services in any calendar quarter after that date.

headings.title: Included and excluded services within one pay period
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and source notes. Applies the half-or-more pay-period rule to include or exclude an individual's entire service during a pay period of up to 31 consecutive days when some services are excluded, except where any service is excluded under subsection 12(8).

headings.title: Exclusion for full-time students at organized summer camps
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 15 and source notes. Excludes services performed by a full-time student in the employ of an organized summer camp for fewer than 13 calendar weeks in the calendar year.

headings.title: Definition of full-time student for summer camp exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 16 (subdivisions (1)–(2)) and source notes. Defines full-time student status for subsection 15 during enrollment or between academic years or terms with prior full-time enrollment and reasonable assurance of succeeding enrollment.

headings.title: Definition of organized summer camp for subsection 15
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 17 (subdivisions (1)–(2)) and source notes. Defines 'organized summer camp' for subsection 15 by either operating no more than seven months in the current and preceding calendar years or meeting the 33⅓% six-month average gross-receipts seasonality test.

headings.title: Remodeling salesperson exclusion and IRS determination exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 18 and source notes (added through A.L. 2010 H.B. 1692 et al.). Excludes remodeling salespersons acting as independent contractors unless the federal IRS determines the contractual relationship with the direct provider is an employer-employee relationship for federal law purposes.

headings.title: Inclusion of Indian tribes as employers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2003 S.B. 194 & 189, effective 5-08-03). Includes any Indian tribe for which service in employment under § 288.034 is performed within the term 'employer'.

headings.title: Covered employment with Indian tribes and exclusions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (L. 2003 S.B. 194 & 189, effective 5-08-03). Includes service for a FUTA § 3306(u) Indian tribe excluded from FUTA solely under § 3306(c)(7) and not otherwise excluded under chapter 288, and applies § 288.034(9) exclusions.

headings.title: Benefit terms and tribal educational institution rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (L. 2003 S.B. 194 & 189). Makes benefits from tribal employment payable on the same terms as other covered service and applies § 288.040(3) educational-service-agency rules to wholly tribally owned and operated educational institutions and agencies.

headings.title: Tribal contributions, reimbursement elections, and surety bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (subdivisions (1)–(8)) and source notes (L. 2003 S.B. 194 & 189). Covers tribal and tribal-unit joint and several liability, contribution versus § 288.090(3) reimbursement elections, billing, surety-bond requirements ($100,000 minimum or prior-year liability), loss and discretionary reinstatement of coverage on 90-day bond default, IRS/USDOL notification, and required bond-deficiency notice disclosures.

headings.title: Consequences of tribal payment delinquency and reinstatement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 (subdivisions (1)–(3)) and source notes (L. 2003 S.B. 194 & 189). Excludes tribal services from employment upon failure to pay billed amounts within 90 days, permits director reinstatement after full payment, and requires immediate IRS and USDOL notification after 90 days from a final delinquency notice.

headings.title: Required disclosures in tribal delinquency notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (subdivisions (1)–(2)) and source notes (L. 2003 S.B. 194 & 189). Specifies warnings required in payment and reporting delinquency notices to Indian tribes or tribal units regarding FUTA tax liability and loss of employer/employment status under subsections 1 and 2.

headings.title: Tribal financing of nonreimbursed extended benefits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes (L. 2003 S.B. 194 & 189). Requires an Indian tribe to finance in full any extended benefits attributable to tribal employment that are not reimbursed by the federal government.

headings.title: Weekly benefit eligibility findings and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1)–(7) and continuation paragraphs) and source notes (L. 1951 p. 564 through A.L. 2026 S.B. 890; St. John's Mercy (2009) annotation). Requires deputy findings on registration, ability/availability and work-search contacts (with substitute-teacher, jury-duty, Trade Act training, and recall exceptions), division reporting and exemptions, one-week waiting period (compensable after 2008 when balance qualifies), 14/28-day claim filing, and reemployment assessment/profiling participation.

headings.title: Misconduct suspensions, ineligibility, and deemed discharges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (through A.L. 2026 S.B. 890). Renders a claimant ineligible for waiting week credit or benefits during weeks of suspension by the most recent employer for work-connected misconduct, and treats suspensions of four weeks or more as discharges. Independent review revised title to cover the second sentence treating suspensions of four weeks or more as discharges in addition to suspension ineligibility.

headings.title: Educational institution benefit restrictions and retroactive pay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (subdivisions (1)–(2)) and source notes. Applies regular benefit terms to § 288.034(7)–(8) service except denying between-term, paid-sabbatical, and holiday-recess benefits to instructional, administrative, noninstructional, and educational-service-agency employees with reasonable assurance, with retroactive payment rights for noninstructional workers not subsequently offered work.

headings.title: Workers' compensation and retirement payment benefit offsets
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (subdivisions (1)–(3)) and source notes. Makes claimants ineligible for or reduces benefits (rounded down to the dollar) based on temporary partial workers' compensation or base-period/chargeable-employer pension or retirement payments, while exempting Social Security and Railroad Retirement payments if the claimant contributed in any way.

headings.title: Other unemployment benefit claims, ineligibility, and exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Denies waiting week credit or benefits for weeks in which a claimant receives or seeks unemployment benefits under another state's or federal law, unless finally determined not entitled to those benefits. Independent review revised title to reflect the explicit statutory exception when the claimant is finally determined not entitled to the other-state or federal benefits.

headings.title: Labor dispute work stoppage, strike rules, and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 (subdivisions (1)–(2)) and source notes, including St. John's Mercy Health System v. Division of Employment Security (2009) upholding the unfair labor practice exception against equal protection challenges. Covers labor-dispute work-stoppage ineligibility, subsequent bona fide permanent employment, separate-department rule, nonparticipation/non-grade exceptions, and strike rules with the NLRB/federal-court unfair-labor-practice exception. Independent review revised title to reflect statutory exceptions (nonparticipation/non-grade-or-class, bona fide subsequent employment, and the NLRB/federal-court unfair labor practice strike exception upheld in St. John's Mercy).

headings.title: Between-season benefit restriction for athletic services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes. Prohibits paying benefits on or after January 1, 1978, based on sports or athletic participation or training services for weeks between successive sport seasons when the individual has reasonable assurance of performing such services in the later season. Independent review revised title to remove "professional athlete," which does not appear in text applying to any individual performing sports or athletic participation or training services.

headings.title: Benefit restrictions based on alien status and proof
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 (introductory text and subdivisions (1)–(2)) and source notes. Prohibits benefits based on an alien's services unless lawfully admitted for permanent residence, lawfully present to perform the services, or permanently residing under color of law (including INA § 212(d)(5)), requires uniform applicant inquiries, and requires preponderance-of-the-evidence proof for denial.

headings.title: Ineligibility during outstanding section 288.380(9) overpayment penalty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and source notes. Renders a claimant ineligible for waiting week credit or benefits for any week in which the claimant has an outstanding penalty assessed for a benefit overpayment under § 288.380(9). Independent review revised title to preserve the exact § 288.380(9) cross-reference without adding the word "fraud" absent from subsection 9's own text.

headings.title: Annual interagency report on work search and reemployment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and source notes. Directs the directors of the division of employment security and office of workforce development to submit an initial October 15, 2006 report and annual December 31 reports to the governor and legislative leaders on work-search verification, 'greathires.org' utilization, and reducing claim duration. Retains archived phrasing 'include, but not limited to'.

headings.title: Electronic and alternate methods for claimant reporting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and source notes (through A.L. 2026 S.B. 890). Permits claimants to satisfy reporting requirements under § 288.040 by internet communication or any other means deemed acceptable by the division of employment security.

headings.title: Definition of war on terror veteran
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (subdivisions (1)–(4)) and source notes (L. 2006 H.B. 1456, A.L. 2007 S.B. 433, A.L. 2008 H.B. 2041, effective 10-01-08). Defines 'war on terror veteran' by Missouri domicile prior to deployment, National Guard or reserve status, post-September 11, 2001 deployment preventing civilian work, prior employment, and a Missouri or federal district court finding of discharge or layoff during or within 30 days after deployment.

headings.title: Weekly benefit amount calculation and maximum cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (effective 10-01-08). Entitles qualifying war on terror veterans, notwithstanding §§ 288.010 to 288.500, to weekly benefits of 8% of highest-quarter wages in the five completed pre-deployment quarters, capped at $1,153.64 per week.

headings.title: Benefit duration and recovery of overpaid benefits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 10-01-08). Sets a 26-week entitlement period for war on terror veteran weekly benefits and directs the division to recover overpayments via billing, state and federal tax-refund setoffs, § 313.321 lottery intercepts, and §§ 288.160, 288.170, and 288.175 collections.

headings.title: Employer administrative penalty and USERRA judgment notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (effective 10-01-08). Imposes a $35,000 administrative penalty (collectible under §§ 288.160 and 288.170) on an employer found by a Missouri or federal district court in Missouri to have taken adverse action due to deployment absence, and directs judicial notice (and permissible res judicata effect) of 38 U.S.C. § 4301 USERRA judgments.

headings.title: Deemed discharge without equivalent post-deployment job offer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (effective 10-01-08). Treats a war on terror veteran as discharged if not offered the same wages, benefits, and a similar work schedule upon return from deployment.

headings.title: War on Terror Unemployment Compensation Fund administration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes (effective 10-01-08). Creates the War on Terror Unemployment Compensation Fund in the state treasury under state treasurer custody, restricts appropriated disbursements to section administration, benefits, and refunds, exempts balances from § 33.080 reversion, and credits investment earnings to the fund.

headings.title: Division rulemaking authority and chapter 536 nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes (effective 10-01-08). Authorizes division rules subject to chapter 536 and § 536.028 and declares the section and chapter 536 nonseverable, invalidating rulemaking grants and post-August 28, 2006 rules if legislative review powers are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Required prior employee notice of workplace testing policy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 10-01-06). headings.title: Admissible testing categories, preemployment tests, and misconduct
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes (effective 10-01-06). headings.title: Collective bargaining agreement exception and legal compliance limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (effective 10-01-06). headings.title: Fraud determinations, penalties, appeals, and overpayment collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 (subdivisions (1)–(5)) and source notes. Effective July 1, 2005, defines claimant or employer benefit fraud, directs deputy repayment and 25% (or 100% repeat) penalty determinations, sets 30-day § 288.190 appeals, governs subsection 14 collection, benefit-only offsets, repayment order (15% of fraud benefits from penalty to unemployment fund, remainder to special fund), and references § 288.160(4) for employer fraud.

headings.title: Forfeiture of benefit rights and wage-credit cancellation for willful falsification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and source notes. Imposes forfeiture of benefit rights and cancellation of prior wage credits (modifiable by the division for good cause) for willful nondisclosure of earnings or disqualifying/material facts, with a presumption of willfulness on signed, certified claims.

headings.title: Benefit debt exemptions and child-support or food-stamp withholding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 (subdivisions (1)–(2), including paragraphs (a)–(k)) and source notes. Voids benefit assignments and exempts unmingled benefits from debt collection except for unemployment necessaries, child-support obligations (Social Security Act Title IV-D), and food-stamp overissuances; sets disclosure, deduction, administrative-cost reimbursement, definitions, and withholding priority (subsection 12/13 overpayments first, then child support, then food stamps).

headings.title: Recovery of overpayments caused by nondisclosure or misrepresentation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and source notes. Makes recipients of improper benefits due to nondisclosure or misrepresentation by themselves or another liable, in the division's discretion, for future-benefit offset or repayment collectible under subsection 14.

headings.title: Recovery of division-error overpayments and small-amount waiver option
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and source notes. Makes recipients of improper benefits due to division error, omission, or lack of knowledge liable after a § 288.190(2) fair-hearing opportunity for offset or subsection 14 repayment, while allowing the division not to process overpayments not exceeding 20% of the maximum weekly benefit amount.

headings.title: Methods for collecting overpaid unemployment compensation benefits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and source notes. Directs pursuing overpaid benefit recovery via billing, state and federal tax-refund setoffs (as permitted by federal law), § 313.321 lottery-winnings intercepts, and §§ 288.160, 288.170, and 288.175 collections.

headings.title: Reciprocal benefit offsets for other states' overpayments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 15 and source notes. Requires deducting another state's or other-state-administered federal unemployment benefit overpayments from Missouri benefits after a § 288.190(2) fair-hearing opportunity, conditioned on a reciprocal recovery agreement with that state.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history (L. 1972 H.B. 1017 through A.L. 2016 H.B. 1530 merged with S.B. 702); verified all fingerprints. Checked post-reversal benefit collection notwithstanding § 288.070(8), back-pay overpayment withholding, division benefit disclosure, and treble damages for obstruction; retained all four titles.

headings.title: Collection of benefits paid pending review after final reversal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1972 H.B. 1017, A.L. 1988 H.B. 1485, A.L. 2006 H.B. 1456, A.L. 2016 H.B. 1530 merged with S.B. 702). Makes benefits paid under § 288.070(7) to which a claimant is later finally determined not entitled collectible under § 288.380(12) and (13), notwithstanding § 288.070(8).

headings.title: Overpayment establishment and employer withholding from back pay awards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (through A.L. 2016 H.B. 1530 merged with S.B. 702). Directs establishing an overpayment for the lesser of a court, agency, or arbitration back-pay award or attributable benefits, and requires employer withholding and remittance after a § 288.190 fair-hearing opportunity.

headings.title: Division disclosure of benefit amounts to employer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Requires the division to provide the employer with the amount of benefits paid to the claimant for subsection 2 withholding.

headings.title: Treble damages for obstructing employer back-pay withholding
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Imposes liability for three times the amount owed to the division, collectible under §§ 288.160 and 288.170, on anyone who interferes with, obstructs, or causes an employer to fail to comply with subsection 2.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 10 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(6) of subsection 4), history/effective date (L. 2004 H.B. 1268 § 1211, effective 1-01-05), and both Revisor footnotes (*Word "is" appears in original rolls. in subsection 6; **"This act" (H.B. 1268 & 1211, 2004)... in subsection 8); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed archived wording ("under/pursuant to this subsection" in subsections 7, 9, and 10) and archived federal citations (15 U.S.C. 1681f and 1681l) are retained faithfully; retained all 10 titles.

headings.title: Division contracts with consumer reporting agencies for wage access
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 2004 H.B. 1268 § 1211, effective 1-01-05; note '**' footnote referencing 'H.B. 1268 & 1211, 2004'). Authorizes contracting with consumer reporting agencies (preferring those with Missouri offices) for secure electronic quarterly wage-report access, limited to FCRA § 604 (15 U.S.C. § 1681b) permissible uses.

headings.title: Eight-quarter limit on released wage information and agency definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes (effective 1-01-05). Limits released data to employing unit names, addresses, and wage amounts for up to the last eight quarters, and incorporates the FCRA § 603(f) definition of 'consumer reporting agency' (retaining archived '15 U.S.C. 1681f' citation).

headings.title: Privacy rules and mandatory prior written consumer consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 1-01-05). Subjects released wage data to Missouri privacy rules, the federal FCRA, and § 288.398, and requires consumer reporting agencies to mandate prior written consent from the individual before any user obtains wage information.

headings.title: Required prominent disclosures in written consumer consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (subdivisions (1)–(6)) and source notes (effective 1-01-05). Lists six prominent disclosures required in the written consent: voluntary nature without credit-denial penalty, specified recipients, authorization requirement, sole transaction purpose, division employer-submitted file access, and authorized recipients' names and addresses.

headings.title: Verification-only restriction on user use of wage information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (effective 1-01-05). Requires consumer reporting agencies to restrict user use solely to verifying previously provided wage or employment data for a specific transaction's underwriting and state or federal fair-credit-reporting obligations.

headings.title: Confidentiality standards, zero division cost, immunity, and fee deposits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes, including Revisor footnote '*Word "is" appears in original rolls.' on 'state and division are* immune'. Directs setting security, audit, net-worth, and insurance standards, bars division costs, allows voiding noncompliant contracts, grants state/division immunity except for willful and wanton misconduct, and dedicates fees solely to trust-fund benefit payments.

headings.title: Civil liability in state court for willful noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes (effective 1-01-05). Makes any person or entity willfully failing to comply with 'any requirement imposed under this subsection' (retaining archived wording) liable to the consumer in Missouri state courts to the same extent as FCRA § 616 (15 U.S.C. § 1681n).

headings.title: Consumer action for injunctive relief in circuit court
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes, including Revisor footnote '**"This act" (H.B. 1268 & 1211, 2004) contains numerous sections. Consult Disposition of Sections table for a definitive listing.' Authorizes a consumer to bring a circuit court action to enjoin a violation of 'this act'.

headings.title: Penalties for obtaining information under false pretenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and source notes (effective 1-01-05). Punishes anyone who knowingly and willfully obtains information 'pursuant to this subsection' (retaining archived wording) from a consumer reporting agency under false pretenses to the same extent as FCRA § 619 (15 U.S.C. § 1681q).

headings.title: Resolution of consumer disputes over completeness or accuracy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and source notes (effective 1-01-05). Directs handling consumer file completeness or accuracy disputes for information obtained 'under this subsection' (retaining archived wording) under FCRA § 611 (retaining archived '15 U.S.C. 1681l' citation).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 19 subsections (including subdivisions of subsections 2, 4, and 12) and history/effective date (L. 1987 S.B. 153 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 844, effective 6-27-14); verified all fingerprints. Confirmed archived stale cross-reference in subsection 13 ("subdivision (3) of subsection 1 of section 288.040", where waiting week is now subdivision (4)) and catchline mismatch in subsection 17 (charging versus § 288.120 rates) are documented faithfully without silent repair; retained all 19 titles.

headings.title: Creation of voluntary Shared Work Unemployment Compensation Program
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1987 S.B. 153 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 844, effective 6-27-14). Creates the voluntary Shared Work Unemployment Compensation Program and authorizes the division to adopt consistent administrative rules and procedures.

headings.title: Shared work program definitions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (subdivisions (1)–(9)) and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Defines nine section-specific terms: affected unit (3+ employees), division, fringe benefit, normal weekly hours of work (lesser of 40 or 12-week average), participating employee, participating employer, shared work benefit, shared work plan, and shared work unemployment compensation program.

headings.title: Employer plan submission, reporting, monitoring, and evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Requires an employer seeking participation to submit a written plan in acceptable form, agree to furnish requested operational reports, and monitor, evaluate, and report plan findings.

headings.title: Division approval criteria for shared work plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (subdivisions (1)–(11)) and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Lists 11 discretionary plan approval criteria: current reports and paid contributions, identified unit and employees, 20%–40% hour reduction for at least 10% of unit employees, continued fringe benefits, layoff-avoidance certification and estimate, employee notice description, legal-compliance certification, and U.S. Secretary of Labor provisions.

headings.title: Written union approval under collective bargaining agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Requires written approval by the collective bargaining agent if any employees participating in a shared work plan are covered by a collective bargaining agreement.

headings.title: Restrictions on seasonal off-season subsidies and holiday-hour overlap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Prohibits approving plans that subsidize seasonal employers off-season, bars initiating benefits for hours overlapping committed holiday pay, and bars denying benefits during holiday weeks unless claiming the same hours on the same day as holiday pay.

headings.title: Thirty-day written decision, review, and reapplication waiting period
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Requires written approval or denial (with reasons) within 30 days of receipt, makes determinations final subject to legal review, and requires waiting at least 45 calendar days after denial to submit a new plan.

headings.title: Revocation and termination of approved shared work plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Permits the division to revoke approval and terminate a shared work plan if not executed according to program terms and intent or if approved based on false or substantially misleading information.

headings.title: Effective date and twelve-month expiration of approved plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Sets plan effectiveness on the first day of the approval week or a later plan-specified date, with expiration on the last day of the twelfth full calendar month after the effective date.

headings.title: Modification of approved shared work plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Allows employers to modify plans for changed conditions with seven days' advance written notice, subject to division reevaluation under subsection 4 (and denial under subsection 7) without altering the original expiration date.

headings.title: Unemployment status of participating employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Deems an affected-unit employee unemployed for § 288.500 in any week worked for fewer than normal weekly hours under an effective approved shared work plan.

headings.title: Weekly eligibility requirements for shared work benefits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 (subdivisions (1)–(4)) and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Conditions shared work benefit eligibility for otherwise eligible claimants on employment in an approved affected unit, availability for normal hours with the participating employer (notwithstanding § 288.040(1)(2)), a 20%–40% hour and wage reduction, and serving a § 288.030 waiting week.

headings.title: Reciprocal waiting-week credit and new initial claim rule
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Credits waiting weeks reciprocally between § 288.040 and subsection 12(4) (retaining archived 'subdivision (3) of subsection 1 of section 288.040' citation), while requiring a waiting week upon filing a new initial claim during a plan's 12-month period.

headings.title: Exemptions from work-search, outside-work refusal, and training disqualifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Bars denying shared work benefits based on availability, active work search, refusing work from non-participating employers, or director-approved training under § 288.055 (including employer-sponsored or WIA 1998 training).

headings.title: Calculation and rounding of weekly shared work benefit amount
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 15 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Calculates weekly shared work benefits as regular WBA minus chapter deductibles (excluding employer wages) multiplied by the plan's full hour-reduction percentage, rounded down to the next lowest dollar.

headings.title: Aggregate benefit-year cap and fifty-two-week limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 16 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Caps combined shared work and regular benefits at the § 288.060 benefit-year maximum and limits shared work benefits to 52 calendar weeks within the plan's 12-month period.

headings.title: Employer account charging for shared work benefits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 17 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Directs charging shared work benefits to participating and other base-period employers in the same manner as regular unemployment benefits under chapter 288 (note: official catchline refers to employer contribution computation, now governed by § 288.120).

headings.title: Exhaustee status and extended benefit eligibility under section 288.062
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 18 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Classifies an individual who exhausts all available shared work and regular benefits in a benefit year as an exhaustee eligible for extended benefits under § 288.062 if otherwise qualified.

headings.title: Severability of federally nonconforming provisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 19 and source notes (effective 6-27-14). Preserves the validity of remaining § 288.500 provisions if the U.S. Secretary of Labor determines any provision does not conform with federal law.
